spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The appendix makes the heuristic kernel match uniform enough for proof by discarding Möbius cancellation, controlling the positive binomial-exponential error through a unimodal envelope, and reducing the sum to a maximum plus an integral.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The proof bounds |R(k)/k-c_k| by replacing |μ(n)| with 1 and summing h(n)=n^-2[exp(-k/n^2)-(1-1/n^2)^k]. Positivity and unimodality give sum h(n) <= max h+integral h; after y=1/x, Gaussian and beta-integral estimates yield a leading (3 sqrt(π)/16)k^-3/2 term with lower-order k^-2, k^-5/2, and k^-3 terms. For k>16 the leading order suffices.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is the quantitative de-Poissonization mechanism. Kernel mismatch is isolated as the sole error object, then continuous integral asymptotics convert local binomial-versus-exponential discrepancy into a uniform coefficient bound.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The central bridge is the positive error profile h(x); unimodal sum-to-integral comparison connects the discrete n-sum to Gaussian and Euler-beta representations whose asymptotics are controllable.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Removing Möbius signs sacrifices possible cancellation and may be non-sharp. The result controls only c_k versus the integer sample R(k)/k and supplies no Riesz growth estimate by itself; exact constants should not be promoted to formal claims without checking the displayed formulas.
directed.uncertainty: Several radicals and fractions are layout-risky in extraction, but the prose and final inequality robustly support the O(k^-3/2) leading rate and the k>16 simplification.
